text:
The goal that decided this one came from the fourth line. William Carrier, the third star's first-star counterpart in our book, backhanded in a feed from Andrei Svechnikov and Sebastian Aho with 5:08 left in the third period to put CAR up 4-3, and Jalen Chatfield sealed the 5-3 win with a snap shot at 19:09. Carrier was drafted 57th overall by the Blues in 2013, and he finished with a goal and an assist on 13:54 of ice time, the least of any CAR skater on the list of top performers.

By our numbers, NYI had the better of the play. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the count of shots, came out almost even, 3.5 for CAR and 3.45 for NYI. Our "deserved to win" figure, the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, gave NYI 52 percent and CAR 48. Brandon Bussi saved 0.45 goals more than an average goalie would have against those chances, while Semyon Varlamov, who faced 38 shots, allowed 0.65 more than expected. NYI also went 0 for 4 on the power play (0.47 expected goals), and Simon Holmstrom had a 37 percent look in the third that Bussi turned away.

CAR scored first, twice in the opening 3:20, and answered each NYI push. Mitchell Chaffee and Brayden Schenn tied it at 2-2, Svechnikov restored the lead a minute later, and Victor Eklund tied it again late in the second. The third belonged to CAR, which out-chanced NYI 1.15 to 0.88 in expected goals that period. Our facts don't include records or streaks for either side, so we'll leave the standings to others. We'd note only that NYI controlled long stretches of the middle period and still left with nothing.
